blocks.text: Arrivals, seats and cruise volumes can be tracked from existing feeds; spread, bookability, jobs and community spend cannot until new data is built or shared.

Stakeholders put data among the top barriers: no approved methodology exists for provincial tourism GDP and jobs (Stakeholder Insights Report, Mar 2026, p37), and no one holds a single view of visitor behaviour (Current State Diagnostic, Dec 2025, p56, p57). Two provincial bodies already hold part of that view. The Provincial Treasury's district reviews print attraction counts, bed-nights and tourist spend as a share of GDPR (Municipal Economic Review and Outlook 2024/25, Cape Metro, p68 to p73; Municipal Economic Review and Outlook 2024/25, West Coast, p126 to p131). The Department of Mobility's Integrated Transport Hub is the province's most comprehensive transport data repository (Western Cape Department of Mobility, draft Provincial Land Transport Framework, Apr 2025, p3-60). The data-sharing protocol under focus area 18 (I16) is the route to closing the gaps below.
